We need a reference-file check and a runner that retains failed cases before
sampling electron-cyclotron (EC) labels. The [Primer](../primer.qmd) explains why
surrogate data needs a defined source; terminology is in the
[Glossary](../glossary.qmd).

We checked the EC reader against a real saved output in the upstream
regression suite: [200 native bins in the saved upstream ITER EC output pass reader and accounting checks]{.claim}[C-152](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-152){.cid .st-measured}. Its power and toroidal-current integrals
agree with the stored totals to floating-point precision. The file identifies
an older solver version. Reading it validates the boundary adapter; it does not
select a project launch, establish current-solver accuracy or produce new labels.
The upstream file is independent of our synthetic fixtures; its accounting
check still uses our reader.

The saved case also shows why current conventions matter: parallel current is
negative while toroidal and ONETWO currents are positive. Preserving the channels
and their signs is necessary before defining a transport-source conversion.

The new pilot runner requires explicit input files, executable, reference/build
identity, case and family IDs, lineage and wall limit. It snapshots the inputs
and binary, retains logs and partial outputs, records failures, and refuses to
overwrite a previous run. A timeout kills the subprocess group. Every retained
regular file has content-bound provenance. A readable output remains draft data;
it is not a physical acceptance result or a training dataset.

[40 focused pilot, reader and Tier A checks pass in full and Tier-A-only modes]{.claim}[C-153](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-153){.cid .st-tested}. Lifecycle tests use fake executables, including failed launches,
nonzero exits, malformed or missing outputs, changed inputs, timeout cleanup,
Tier B lineage rejection and CLI failure reporting. Historical full-suite
statistics remain separate from these focused checks.

Compiler and NetCDF modules are available. The checked compiler configuration
does not resolve the plotting library required by the upstream build, so that
dependency or a documented executable remains needed. No reference build, solver
execution or cluster job was performed at this checkpoint. The
[build](32-genray-build-and-pilot-request.qmd) and
[numerical execution](34-genray-corrected-numerical-pilot.qmd) follow separately.
Production baseline and pedestal-boundary choices
remain with the owner; the independent ITER port is unchanged.
M3 remains in progress.
